risks.description: AC-1 (a document field that conflicts with the system of record is surfaced as a conflict and never silently overwrites it) cannot be exercised with the approved toolset. The reconciler (reconciliation.reconcile_load / extraction_bridge.reconciliation_from_extraction) that produces VARIANCE reasons and keeps the rate/source-of-truth side untouched is in-process only; there is no approved command or 8001 endpoint that ingests a carrier document with a conflicting field and persists the outcome to workflow_runs for inspection. The single most load-bearing AC (weight 3) is therefore unverified in this wave.
risks.basis: Active unit U-EV-4 AC: 'a document field that conflicts with the system of record is surfaced as a conflict and never silently overwrites it'; implemented in src/freight_recon/extraction_bridge.py + reconciliation.py, no approved driver.

risks.description: AC-2 (a document missing a required field yields a stated missing-evidence result rather than a guess) is unverified. extraction.py sets absent fields to null/confidence 0 and extraction_bridge.REQUIRED_CONFIDENCE_FIELDS forces NEEDS_REVIEW, but nothing driveable feeds a document missing a required field and reads back the persisted 'missing-evidence' outcome/reason, so a regression to guessing would not be caught.
risks.basis: U-EV-4 AC: 'a document missing a required field yields a stated missing-evidence result rather than a guess'; REQUIRED_CONFIDENCE_FIELDS in extraction_bridge.py.

risks.description: AC-4 (an inference is never presented as a known fact) is unverified. The known/inferred split (deterministic agreed_rate_total vs model-extracted invoice side; low_confidence_required flags) exists in code, but there is no driveable surface or persisted-provenance field a scenario can inspect to prove an inferred value is not rendered as known.
risks.basis: U-EV-4 AC: 'an inference is never presented as a known fact'; reconciliation.agreed_rate_total docstring + extraction_bridge low_confidence_required.

risks.description: AC-3's vision-layer half (an unparseable *document* is refused with a reason and changes no state) is only partially reachable. The callback boundary lets me prove an unverifiable *token* is refused without committing an effect, but the actual unparseable-PDF path (document_identifier.extract_pdf_identifiers / extraction.extract_from_pdf returning error=... FAILED) is not driveable, so a bad scan silently mutating state at the extraction layer would not be caught here.
risks.basis: U-EV-4 AC: 'an unparseable document is refused with a reason and changes no state'; extraction.py/document_identifier.py fail-closed error paths.

risks.description: A malformed but token-shaped input to POST /actions/signed may raise an uncaught decode error (only DeliveryExpiredError/DeliverySignatureError/WorkflowError are caught) and surface as an HTTP 500/traceback instead of a stated refusal — a dead-end rather than the reasoned refusal AC-3 requires. Scenario UEV4-W1-01 probes exactly this.
risks.basis: src/freight_recon/action_callback.py handle_signed_action_callback try/except only catches three exception types around submit_signed_action.

scenarios.title: Unverifiable signed action is refused with a stated reason, not a 500, and commits nothing
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the deployed decision-application boundary with an unverifiable input and confirm it is refused WITH A REASON while no external effect is committed to the system of record.
scenarios.rationale: AC-3 requires an unparseable input be refused with a reason and change no state; the callback is the only driveable path that applies a decision to workflow.sqlite3, so a crash/500 or a silent apply here is a direct AC-3/AC-1 violation.
scenarios.generating_risk: a malformed/unverifiable input is swallowed or crashes (500/traceback) instead of yielding a stated refusal that commits nothing
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-EV-4 AC: an unparseable document is refused with a reason and changes no state
scenarios.isolation_note: Submits only an unverifiable token; a refusal commits nothing and the persisted_state_checks confirm no external effect grant was created, so it cannot contaminate the next scenario.

persisted_state_checks.name: no external effect verified
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM effect_grants WHERE state='VERIFIED'"

persisted_state_checks.name: no external effect even attempted
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM effect_grants WHERE state IN ('ATTEMPTED','CLAIMED','VERIFIED')"

scenarios.title: Missing action token yields a stated missing-input refusal, not a silent success
scenarios.purpose: Confirm that an input missing its required credential is answered with an explicit stated-missing result rather than proceeding or guessing, and changes no state.
scenarios.rationale: Mirrors AC-2's shape at the driveable boundary: a missing required element must produce a stated result, never a silent proceed; the email-action route with no token is the only approved way to observe this against the system of record.
scenarios.generating_risk: a request missing its required token is treated as valid / proceeds silently instead of returning a stated 'missing' refusal
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-EV-4 AC: an unparseable document is refused with a reason and changes no state
scenarios.isolation_note: A GET with no token never reaches submit; nothing is written, and the state check confirms no committed effect.

persisted_state_checks.name: no external effect verified after missing-token request
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM effect_grants WHERE state='VERIFIED'"

scenarios.title: A non-parseable request body is refused cleanly and commits no effect
scenarios.purpose: Drive the boundary with a body that is neither valid JSON nor a token-bearing form and confirm a stated refusal with no state mutation — the 'unparseable input, no state change' invariant on the deployed surface.
scenarios.rationale: AC-3 demands unparseable input be refused with a reason and change no state; a garbage body must not be coerced into an applied action, and the effect ledger must remain dark.
scenarios.generating_risk: an unparseable request body is partially interpreted and mutates state, or errors into a 500 instead of a stated refusal
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-EV-4 AC: an unparseable document is refused with a reason and changes no state
scenarios.isolation_note: Garbage body cannot carry a valid token, so submit is never reached; state checks confirm nothing committed.

persisted_state_checks.name: effect ledger still shows no verified external write
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM effect_grants WHERE state IN ('ATTEMPTED','CLAIMED','VERIFIED')"

assumptions: The 'callback' service on http://127.0.0.1:8001 is bound to the system-of-record database at data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 (the only approved sqlite3 target), so refusals and effects on that surface are observable there.

The deployment ships 'dark' (P4/R-07, governed route kernel is None → ROUTE_NOT_CONFIGURED): no real external write is ever VERIFIED, so a standing safety invariant is that effect_grants has zero rows in ATTEMPTED/CLAIMED/VERIFIED. A scenario that ever observes such a row indicates a silent overwrite of the system of record.

Slack routes (/slack/*) are disabled in the harness because no Slack signing secret is configured, so only /actions/signed and /email/action are reachable without secrets; the scenarios use only those.

effect_grants.state literals are exactly {GRANTED,CLAIMED,ATTEMPTED,VERIFIED,FAILED,EXPIRED_UNCLAIMED,REVOKED,UNKNOWN_OUTCOME} (migrations/phase2_tenant_first.py), with VERIFIED being the terminal 'external effect committed' state.
unresolved_questions: The core U-EV-4 behaviour — vision extraction of a carrier document reconciled against the shipment record, with conflict surfacing (AC-1), stated missing-evidence results (AC-2), and known-vs-inferred labeling (AC-4) — is implemented in-process (extraction.py, extraction_bridge.py, reconciliation.py) but is NOT reachable via any approved command or port-8001 endpoint. Is there an ingestion endpoint or an approved CLI that reconciles a *supplied* document (or corpus fixture) and persists the outcome/reason to workflow_runs so AC-1/AC-2/AC-4 can be driven black-box? Without one, three of the four ACs (two of them weight-3) are unverifiable this wave.

Where is the 'known fact vs inference' provenance persisted for a reconciled document (workflow_runs.reason, an audit_events.payload_json, or an extraction audit payload)? A scenario needs a concrete persisted field to assert that an inferred value is never rendered as a known fact.

No approved command resets or seeds driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3, so 'changes no state' can only be asserted against the absolute dark-deployment invariant (no ATTEMPTED/CLAIMED/VERIFIED effect grants), not against a per-request row delta. Is a fixture/reset or a baseline-capture command available so before/after mutation of workflow_runs and delivery_action_claims can be verified directly?

Should the token-boundary refusal invariants I can drive here be treated as satisfying AC-3, or only as adjacent effect-boundary safety checks? The AC is literally about an unparseable *carrier document* at the extraction layer; I have deliberately not claimed the callback-token scenarios discharge the document-layer AC.
